name: Kisi
catalog_citation: Gray, Hazel. 2018. Kisi Phonology and Morphophonology. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 38. SIL International. (PDF, 62 pp.)
catalog_locator: sec. 5 'Stress', p. 32; also Abstract (front matter) and sec. 6.2.1.4 'Vowel length transfer'
catalog_quote: Kisi, like its northern neighbour Nyakyusa, does not have contrastive pitch. It is purely a stress language where stress is always realised on the penultimate syllable of the word. This stress is realised as an increased intensity over the relevant syllable and added length in the vowel of the stressed syllable. The intensity increase may be seen by examining the yellow line in figure 5.1, which shows the spectrogram of the word /lisoˈsolo/ ‘louse’. Pitch may play a part in indicating the stressed syllable however it is not always the case that the highest pitch is found during the stressed syllable. ... [Abstract:] Kisi (Bantu G67, Tanzania) is a seven-vowel language with contrastive vowel length and predictable stress on the penultimate syllable of the word. ... audit.reasoning: The coding (fixed penultimate, weight-blind, no contrastive pitch) rests on a 2018 SIL phonology monograph that is the most extensive and only descriptive source Glottolog lists for kisi1243; we hold the PDF and the deciding quotation is verbatim in sec. 5, supported by the Abstract and sec. 6.2.1.4. The source is modern, fieldwork-based, and gives instrumental illustration (intensity trace, PU vowel durations). No competing description of Kisi prosody was found in Glottolog 5.1 or Crossref; the one candidate (Ngonyani's Kikisi grammar) is an unpublished Ms of unknown availability. Only housekeeping: the locator should read p. 31 (printed) / PDF p. 37 rather than p. 32. No recode indicated. Nothing was fetched sources, so no files were written under
